title: Patterns & Weak Signals — Aria Lim (initial notes)
content:
Context:
- 45m initial technical screen (remote). Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference serving).
- Candidate referred by an ex-Redwood IC. Resume: 7+ years infra/ML infra, last two roles at small infra startups.

Quick take (one-liner):
- Strong practical instincts; leans toward pragmatic engineering tradeoffs rather than academic deep dives. Good on operationalizing models and debugging tail latency issues; weaker on low-level kernel/quantization math.

What I liked (evidence):
- Concrete examples: led a production rollout that reduced 95p latency by switching to async batching + per-customer route caching (gave metrics: 95p from 420ms -> 280ms). Walked through tradeoffs (cache invalidation, staleness windows).
- Clear incident narrative: described a P1 where KV cache corruption surfaced under burst traffic — could reproduce, isolated via tracing, hotfix (restart + incremental migration). Shows SRE mindset.
- Ops-first mental model: asked about observability signals (token-level latency distributions, CPU vs GPU stalls, memmap churn). Proposed practical dashboards.

Concerns / weak signals (pattern-level):
- Tendency to default to "add more infra" (more pods, larger GPUs) rather than software-level optimizations when probed deeper. Not a dealbreaker but may bias cost decisions.
- Less confident on model optimization primitives: when asked about quantization tradeoffs (INT8 vs FP16), discussion stayed high-level; couldn't articulate concrete microbenchmarks or kernel selection heuristics.
- Limited exposure to multi-tenant routing and soft-fallback policies — has ideas but lacking implementation detail.

Behavioral signals:
- Collaborative and candid. Owned mistakes in past postmortems.
- Asks good clarifying questions; not defensive when challenged.

Scorecard (rough, out of 5, with short rationale):
- System design / architecture: 4/5 (clear designs, cares about observability & operability)
- Debugging & incident response: 5/5 (strong, concrete examples)
- Performance optimization (runtime internals): 3/5 (good heuristics, lacks low-level kernel detail)
- Communication & collaboration: 4/5 (effective, concise)
- Culture / team fit: 4/5 (SRE-ish, pragmatic)

Concrete examples / quotes I noted:
- "We introduced a 200ms batching window but only for background jobs; latency-sensitive routes had a 5-10 token micro-batch path." (good granularity)
- When asked about memory blowups with KV caches: "We key-sharded cache and kept hot keys pinned to a small pool; eviction was LRU with manual pin overrides for critical customers." (operational).

Suggested follow-ups for next round (if advancing):
- Deep dive on a perf ticket: give them a synthetic micro-benchmark (simple transformer forward pass) and ask how they'd profile and decide between kernel choices, quantization, and batching policies. Look for ability to form experiments and success metrics.
- Pair on a short incident triage exercise: provide traces/metrics and ask them to prioritize mitigations. Evaluate their prioritization and communication to stakeholders.

Red flags to probe further if we proceed:
- Cost tradeoff conservatism: test whether they'd accept small model accuracy regressions for large cost wins (we need someone comfortable with measured regressions for economic gains).
- Kernel-level familiarity: ask a few pointed questions about attention memory layouts, KV cache memory patterns, and quantization-induced degredation modes.

Recommendation (tentative):
- Move to an on-site / take-home pair session focused on runtime perf and triage. Strong candidate for our SRE/Runtime hybrid track, but hire contingent on demonstrated practical knowledge on perf experiments.

Action items (for me):
- Draft targeted take-home perf exercise and share with Eliot by 2025-02-18.
- Add a 30m kernel-level probe question to interviewer guide (Riley).
- Send quick sync message to hiring manager summarizing gut + requested evidence.

Notes to self / loose thoughts: 
- Candidate might excel in Dedicated/Private deployment challenges (customer isolation, SLA-focused rollouts).
- Might pair well with someone strong in kernels/quantization (complementary skills).
- Consider offering a pair-week trial if we get to final loops (small paid contractor week) to see hands-on work.

Unresolved questions I want answered in next loop:
- Has Aria written or maintained CUDA or Triton kernels? If yes, which ones and with what perf characteristics?
- Specific microbench results for quantized vs float runs (throughput, memory footprint, 95p latency).
- Ownership scope at previous startup: end-to-end or only infra orchestration?

End of notes.
